chapter: Howard McGhee's band and bebop in LA
title: How big the Lincoln was; Bill Robinson and Orpheum theatres
summary: The Lincoln as less consistent than the Apollo, the Bill Robinson Theatre and shows at the Orpheum.

story.theme_name: Medicine shows, minstrels, circuses and the black theater circuit
story.community_name: On the road with minstrel, carnival and tent shows

blocks.x: I think ....(?).... compare the Lincoln to the Apollo, saying that the Lincoln was to Los Angeles what the Apollo was to New York.
But was it really that big?

Well, it wasn't that big, because they didn't run a consistent policy. When I came out here, they would just bring in an act occasionally. Like, that's where I first saw Sammy Davis with the Will Mastin Trio, and they were living down at the Morris Hotel down on Fifth Street during that time -- right west of Central Avenue. And I saw several acts in there. But it wasn't as big like the Apollo in New York.

They also had another theatre down on 43rd and Central called the Bill Robinson Theatre, with the greatest seats I ever sat in in a theatre -- in this little theatre, you know. They had loge seats where you'd just sink into them, you know... [LAUGHS]
[INAUDIBLE COMMENT] the Lincoln Theatre had main attractions.

Well, it was going when I got here, but it didn't last too much longer after I got here. No, it didn't last too much longer. But it was well established through the years out here, but it was only that Eastern circle that people really catered to ...(? )...
They also had a show down at the Orpheum Theatre down on Broadway, near Ninth Street. Because that's the first place...

Well, the Million-Dollar came later, when they... That's where I saw the Boogie-Woogie child piano prodigy, Sugar Cane Robinson. Remember him? With Gerald Wilson's orchestra on the bill. Also I first saw Roy Hamilton. Remember him, Roy Hamilton? Fine, fine vocalist. But before...
